proposals.title: Product engineering under ambiguity (0-to-1)
proposals.description: Turning ambiguous requirements into working software, including helping determine what to build, not just how. Spans product definition through production in early-stage and unspecified technical environments.

evidence.note: Explicitly names product engineering under ambiguity and shipping in 0-to-1 environments as strongest areas.
Owned email-to-decision-intelligence workflow from product definition through production.

proposals.title: AI application engineering
proposals.description: Building production LLM-powered product features: tool calling, structured/schema-constrained generation, validation and failure handling for non-conforming output, and connecting models to application and organizational context.

evidence.note: Schema-constrained generation with validate/accept/retry/repair/reject boundary between model output and app state.
Tool calling, context design, validation, failure handling for the strategic assistant.
Summarizes direct production LLM feature experience.

proposals.title: AI context and retrieval design
proposals.description: Designing what models see at runtime: page/organization-level provided context, selective tool-based retrieval, and assembling task-specific context from persistent product state rather than indiscriminately loading history.

evidence.note: Two-source runtime context: provided state plus selective tool calls.
Context assembled per operation from persistent user state; application owns context selection.

proposals.title: Third-party API integration and OAuth
proposals.description: Implementing and maintaining production integrations across many external systems: OAuth flows, token lifecycle, REST APIs, pagination, error handling, and mapping external state into internal application models.

evidence.note: Roughly nine external systems including Microsoft Graph, DocuSign, HubSpot; OAuth and token lifecycle.
Four social platform APIs with differing identifiers, schemas, access models, and rate limits.

proposals.title: Cross-system production debugging
proposals.description: Diagnosing production failures that span application state, backend workflows, payment systems, and third-party services by reasoning across both sides of a boundary rather than treating API calls in isolation.

evidence.note: Failures crossing application, workflow, payment, and external service state; live customers.
Integration failures at system boundaries: expired auth, unexpected external state, doc/behavior mismatches.

proposals.title: Application data modeling
proposals.description: Designing data structures and access patterns around how the application consumes data, including normalization layers for heterogeneous external data and flexible persistence for evolving AI-generated state with contracts where correctness matters.

evidence.note: Restructured data around application access patterns at production scale.
Persistence split between durable domain concepts and flexible AI-generated structures with Zod validation boundaries.

proposals.title: Permissions and delegated authorization
proposals.description: Designing authorization models including delegated account access where one user acts on another's behalf without credential sharing, with role-scoped resources and operations.

evidence.note: Delegated access for managers, labels, collaborators with role-scoped permissions.
Lists application data modeling and permissions/authorization among strongest areas.

proposals.title: Marketplace payments engineering
proposals.description: Implementing connected-account payment flows: onboarding, payout eligibility, transaction state coordination between application and payment provider, and correctness under incomplete or disagreeing state.

evidence.note: Stripe Connect onboarding, payouts, and transaction-state coordination for marketplace flow.

proposals.title: Recurring background workflows at scale
proposals.description: Designing server-side scheduled processing under API quotas, execution limits, and cost constraints: scheduling, batching, refresh frequency, and moving work across client/server and service boundaries.

evidence.note: Recurring ingestion reworked for scale: split workflows, adjusted frequency/volume, moved logic across boundaries.
Owned email-to-decision-intelligence pipeline with signal selection over inbox data.

proposals.title: Cross-platform application architecture
proposals.description: Structuring products as shared backends with multiple clients (web and native mobile), monorepo organization, shared contracts, and behavioral parity without duplicated products.

evidence.note: Turborepo monorepo, shared TypeScript/Zod contracts, web/mobile parity checks over one backend.
Architected Next.js web plus Expo/React Native mobile over shared Convex backend.

proposals.title: Choosing implementation boundaries
proposals.description: Deciding where functionality lives — low-code vs conventional stacks, standalone apps vs embedded features, client vs server, custom code vs external services — and executing migrations between them while preserving product behavior.

evidence.note: Bubble-to-TypeScript/Supabase transition; standalone Next.js assistant boundary choice.
Moved selected logic to JavaScript/external services and changed client/server boundaries.

proposals.title: Agentic engineering process design
proposals.description: Establishing team-wide AI-assisted development: shared technical context for humans and agents, agent-based contribution workflows with engineer review, CI/CD and test controls, evals, and task decomposition/model selection by cost and complexity.

evidence.note: Initiated process: shared docs, agent-assisted features, review, testing, CI/CD, evals, model selection.
Expanded development beyond engineering while strengthening documentation, review, testing, delivery controls.

proposals.title: Model-independent AI architecture
proposals.description: Separating model/provider configuration from prompts, application state, output shape, validation, and UI so inference can change independently of workflows — treating model choice as configuration, not architecture.

evidence.note: Model switching and bring-your-own-AI with provider config decoupled from workflow concerns.

proposals.title: Whole-system reasoning
proposals.description: Reasoning across product behavior, data, APIs, frontend state, permissions, and backend workflows as one system: where data moves, which system owns which responsibility, what can fail, and what tradeoffs result.

evidence.note: Names whole-system reasoning explicitly as a strongest area.
Learned engineering from abstractions downward; thinks first about system behavior and responsibility ownership.

proposals.title: Learning velocity in unfamiliar systems
proposals.description: Rapidly building mental models of unfamiliar technologies via documentation, existing code, and AI-accelerated investigation, then validating implementations — enabling productivity without prior stack familiarity.

evidence.note: Explicit claim with C++/JUCE as recent evidence of range, not specialization.

proposals.title: Consumer product and interaction design
proposals.description: Designing and iterating on end-user product experience: interaction models, onboarding, adaptive interfaces derived from user state, and friction reduction based on actual repeated daily use.

evidence.note: Repeated personal use drives information hierarchy, input reduction, friction removal.
Derived daily interface from user state with temporal/derived-state management.

proposals.title: Product analytics instrumentation
proposals.description: Instrumenting products across web, server, and native surfaces with event models tied to application behavior, enabling inspection of whether users progress through the core product loop.

evidence.note: PostHog across browser, server, and React Native covering onboarding, coaching, failures, exceptions.

proposals.title: Production ownership for live systems
proposals.description: Operating and evolving systems serving active customers and real transactions, where changes must preserve existing marketplace, payment, and data-ingestion behavior.

evidence.note: Worked on live systems with thousands of users and real transactions; changes had to preserve behavior.
Operated payments, delegated access, and ingestion in production at marketplace scale.
